purpose: Barn concept exploration; these prompts are not runtime metadata or approved art anchors.

attempts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: one EAST-FACING pixel-art barn sprite study for our Stardew Valley rotation mod.
Input image 1 is the actual SOUTH-facing Barn atlas: preserve THIS building's weathered warm-brown curved/gambrel shingle roof, red vertical-board walls, ochre timber frame, narrow wooden human door, wide animal doorway, and modest lean-to structure. Only the top 112x112 is the building; the bottom 16-pixel strip is loose animated-door artwork and must NOT appear in the result. This is not the red-roof Shed.
Input image 2 is a ground-plan reference, not a drawing style reference. Use only its EAST panel.
Redraw the same building rotated 90 degrees in the WORLD, keeping the familiar elevated Stardew camera looking from the south. Its ground footprint is 4 tiles wide across the screen and 7 tiles deep. Ground axes remain horizontal and vertical; do not turn the footprint into an isometric diamond, and do not rotate the original bitmap.
The EAST entrance wall lies on the RIGHT side of the screen. The wide animal doorway is halfway up that right edge; the narrow human door is nearer its bottom end. The lower/south-facing wall has NO doorway. Slightly cheat the side-wall projection to make the right-facing openings readable while preserving their ground positions. Keep the lean-to attached without adding an arbitrary platform.
Composition: ONE isolated sprite, tall narrow portrait, actual transparent PNG alpha background. Target a 64x160 native-pixel design shown at exactly 8x nearest-neighbor magnification, 512x1280 output. On the native design the ground rectangle extends from (0,48) to (64,160); human threshold target (64,136); animal threshold target (64,96). These coordinates guide the redraw, not visible labels.
Style: match the source's modest density, bold dark brown pixel outline, limited warm brown/red/ochre palette, hand-placed small pixel clusters and stepped edges. Compact in-game sprite, not an elaborate new fantasy building. No smooth gradients, antialiasing, glossy 3D, photorealism, or excessive fine texture.
No terrain, no lawn, no scenery, no characters, no animals, no labels, no grids, no guide marks, no sprite sheet, no extra doors, no unattached objects, and no painted checkerboard. Return only the new east-facing building on genuine transparency.

Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: corrected EAST-facing barn sprite concept.
Image 1 is the edit target. Image 2 is the original south-facing barn, a style/architecture reference only. Image 3 is the exact ground-plan reference; use its EAST panel.
Correct the projection of image 1 so it is suitable for a fixed-camera top-down tile game. Preserve the weathered brown gambrel shingles, red timber walls, lean-to, and TWO right-hand openings: large animal entry midway along the right side, small human door toward the lower end. The lower/south wall remains CLOSED.
The building footprint must be a tall RECTANGLE aligned to the image axes: width 4 tiles, depth 7 tiles. Its right ground edge is VERTICAL, not a diagonal receding right edge. Place both door thresholds on that same vertical right ground boundary. The bottom ground edge is horizontal. Draw vertical wall posts upward from their ground positions, never slanting sideways. Gently flattened game projection rather than an isometric architectural rendering. Keep the roof physically coherent, with its ridge running west-east/across the screen after the world rotation; don't place a front-facing arched gable on the closed south side. Do not rotate the pixel image itself.
Simplify to the original reference's small sprite detail level: crisp deliberately placed square pixel clusters, limited colors, hard pixel edges and no painterly/blurred texture.
Canvas: 1024x2048 portrait. A conceptual 96x192 native grid at 10x scale occupies the centered 960x1920 area with 32px side margins and 64px top/bottom margins. The ground footprint is a 64x112 native rectangle starting at native (16,64); human threshold native (80,152); animal threshold native (80,112). No visible coordinate marks, no diagram.
IMPORTANT: remove the painted gray checkerboard. Return a PNG with a real transparent alpha channel outside the building and through open door gaps. Do not replace it with white, black, checkerboard pixels, terrain, or a drop-shadow card. One building only, no text, no additional doors, people or scenery.

Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: NORTH-FACING barn, normal opaque appearance, one pixel-art concept.
Image 1 is the actual Stardew Valley Barn atlas. Use ONLY its top 112x112 building; the bottom strip contains spare door animation parts, do not draw those. Keep the same humble weathered curved/gambrel BROWN shingle roof, red board walls and ochre wooden frame. Do not replace it with the red-roof Shed.
Image 2 is the ground layout reference, use its NORTH panel. It explains where the real entrances are, not the visual style.
Turn THIS building 180 degrees in the world. Keep the fixed elevated game camera looking northward from the south. We now see the BACK of the barn. Its near, lower wall must be entirely closed red timber with no doors, no fake doorway, and no sign suggesting entry there. The two actual entrances are on the FAR/NORTH edge at the TOP of the ground footprint and should be hidden behind the opaque roof and upper walls in this normal state.
The small human door is at the far edge near the right end; the broad animal opening is at the far edge left of center. Only small far-edge ground hints may be visible beyond the roof, not floating upright doors on the roof. Relocate the attached lean-to consistently to the left side after turning 180 degrees.
Composition: a single compact 7x4 tile barn from the standard Stardew top-down/front camera, squared ground axes, horizontal near-wall base. Moderate overhead view, no isometric diamond, no landscape perspective, no twist or rotate of the bitmap. Keep the barn's existing architectural proportions.
Style: original game's low-resolution pixel sprite, clear limited brown/red palette, dark one-pixel outline and stepped square pixels. Avoid painterly fine noise, airbrush, shiny 3D and gradients.
Present this DESIGN STUDY on a completely uniform pale gray background (#e4e7eb), without a checkerboard. No labels or diagrams, no people, animals, props, terrain or grass. One full building, comfortable small margin. This is the opaque state for a later matched reveal edit.

Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: NORTH-facing barn proximity REVEAL concept, matched to the opaque view.
Image 1 is the exact edit target, an opaque NORTH-facing barn. Preserve its outer silhouette, camera, footprint, attached lean-to location, and centered framing. Image 2 is the precise ground layout guide; use only the NORTH panel. Image 3 is the original Barn atlas to preserve its door and timber details, not its SOUTH-facing layout.
Make a selective cutaway/fade demonstration of image 1. The large roof and upper parts of the near wall become faint, as if at about 20% opacity, while their outlines still explain the barn's shape. Keep a clearly visible low wall base/outline along the entire NEAR/BOTTOM edge. That edge is CLOSED: absolutely NO doorway, steps or passage through it.
Reveal the TWO REAL entrances on the FAR/NORTH edge of the ground footprint, which lies behind the faded roof. The broad animal entrance is LEFT OF CENTER, and the small wooden human door is NEAR THE RIGHT END. They sit along the SAME far horizontal ground line, about halfway down the overall building silhouette, NOT along the bottom/near wall. Their posts rise vertically from that far ground line. Keep the openings, frames and thresholds crisp and opaque. Do not put doors on the roof or invent a new front door.
Include a small attached pictogram sign ON the far human door frame, and just a short plank approach extending NORTH/upward away from that human threshold. No freestanding sign or terrain decoration. Show enough of the unobstructed far approach to communicate how a player reaches the door. The interior need not have furniture or a floor texture: this is showing exterior entrance accessibility through faded occluders, not redesigning the indoor map.
Use the same brown/red/ochre pixel-art materials and lighting. Keep the lower wall's blocked boundary obvious; the entry's north approach remains visibly separate from the blocked footprint. Foreground wall posts must not obscure the real far entrances.
Output one whole reveal-state building at the SAME frame size and position as image 1 on its existing pale-gray backdrop. Fading is illustrative compositing for this concept, not a claim to deliver separate alpha layers. No text, arrows, grids, people, animals, furniture, extra doors, courtyard, or checkerboard.

Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: corrected north-facing barn Reveal concept.
Image 1 is the edit target. Image 2 is its matching normal opaque view; preserve that silhouette, framing and camera exactly. Image 3 is the ground-plane NORTH guide.
Fix ONE structural misunderstanding in image 1: the far entrances currently look like an upper-storey balcony above an opaque lower wall. They must visibly sit on the SAME GROUND PLANE as the barn, with the camera looking through faded occluding walls.
Keep the roof faint. Also fade the WHOLE upper portion of the near/bottom red wall to approximately 15% visibility, including its gable and high boards. Retain ONLY a low, thin wall-base strip and its closed near-edge outline at stronger visibility, approximately 6 native pixels high. Do not leave a tall solid red wall hiding the depth of the ground plane. Keep a faint indication of the original wall's upper silhouette so the structure remains comprehensible.
Keep the wide animal opening and small human door in their current FAR/UPPER positions, but remove the broad horizontal ledge under them. No elevated stage, balcony, mezzanine or second storey. Let a simple subdued ground-colored plane continue from their thresholds toward the near base, seen through the faded walls, clearly showing that both thresholds and the near base belong to the same ground level. This is exterior occlusion, not a new playable indoor courtyard.
The small human door stays on the far right, the large animal opening left of center, the small sign attached next to the human frame. These entrances remain crisp. No extra door or opening in the near/bottom wall.
REMOVE the tall ladder-like stack of planks above the human door. Leave no ladder or stair. Any ground approach hint must be only two short horizontal boards lying FLAT northward/upward outside the far threshold, with shallow foreshortening. It must not look like a vertical structure growing from the door lintel.
Same pixel-art brown roof/red timber/ochre frame, same plain background, same canvas, one matched reveal view, no text, people, animals, arrows or grid. This is an illustrative flattened concept; do not paint a checkerboard.
